hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street obscures sightlines between pedestrians and approaching vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the visible block.

hazards.name: Lack of Designated Crossings
hazards.description: The absence of marked crosswalks forces pedestrians to cross at unmarked locations without priority or visibility aids.
hazards.location_in_image: Entire roadway length visible.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Trash bins and other residential items are placed on the narrow walkway, reducing the effective clear width.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right sidewalks in the foreground and mid-ground

hazards.name: Litter and Debris
hazards.description: Scattered trash and debris in the gutter and on the sidewalk surface can create minor trip hazards.
hazards.location_in_image: In the gutter and on the sidewalk in front of the houses.

hazards.name: Absence of Sidewalk
hazards.description: There is no dedicated space for pedestrians, forcing them to share the roadway with motor vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Entire foreground and midground along the house frontages

hazards.name: Visual and Physical Obstruction
hazards.description: Large parked vehicles block sightlines between residents exiting their homes and drivers on the street, while also physically blocking the path.
hazards.location_in_image: Parked pickup truck and SUV in the foreground

hazards.name: Unmarked Wide Roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings on a wide street encourages higher vehicle speeds and unpredictable lane positioning.
hazards.location_in_image: Center roadway extending into the distance

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking blocks sightlines between pedestrians, particularly children, and approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the block

hazards.name: Lack of sidewalk buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the curb and parked vehicles with no physical buffer or planting strip.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the entire visible sidewalk edge

hazards.name: Potential for high vehicle speeds
hazards.description: The straight, wide roadway without visible traffic calming measures may encourage higher vehicle speeds in a residential area.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway center

hazards.name: Narrow Walkway
hazards.description: Building stairs and the utility pole significantly reduce the effective width of the sidewalk, making it difficult for two people to pass or for those with mobility aids.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Crossing Infrastructure
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks or curb ramps are visible at the approaching intersection, forcing pedestrians to cross in unprotected space.
hazards.location_in_image: Intersection in the middle ground

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking creates a visual barrier between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the street where cars are parked.

hazards.name: Narrow and Obstructed Walkway
hazards.description: The effective width of the sidewalk is reduced by residential stoops and stairs, forcing pedestrians into a narrow path.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both sides of the street where buildings meet the sidewalk

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) at intersections to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers by moving the waiting area past the line of parked cars.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or cushions to physically enforce low speeds on this residential block.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crossings with high-visibility paint and signage to clearly define pedestrian priority areas.

interventions.title: Sidewalk and Curb Construction
interventions.description: Install a standard-width raised sidewalk with a vertical curb to provide a dedicated and protected space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Parking Management and Enforcement
interventions.description: Implement clear parking regulations and physical barriers like bollards to prevent vehicles from parking on the pedestrian path.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to improve visibility and safety for pedestrians using the corridor at night.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the intersection to reduce crossing distance and improve sightlines by preventing parking too close to the corner.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Green Infrastructure
interventions.description: Add street trees to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway while narrowing the perceived street width.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Increase the overall width of the sidewalk to accommodate both the utility infrastructure and a clear pedestrian through-zone.

interventions.title: Utility Relocation
interventions.description: Relocate utility poles to a dedicated furniture zone or underground them to remove physical barriers from the walkway.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Planting street trees would provide a vertical element to narrow the driver's field of vision, naturally slowing traffic while improving the pedestrian experience.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strips
interventions.description: Introduce a furniture zone with street trees or planters to provide a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and vehicles.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near potential crossing points to improve sightlines for both drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening and Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Expand the sidewalk or implement curb extensions to incorporate utility poles into a furniture zone, ensuring a clear and accessible walking path.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or speed cushions to ensure vehicle speeds remain low in this residential context.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct a raised, paved sidewalk with a curb to provide a safe, dedicated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Parking Restrictions/Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near residential access points to improve visibility and provide clear paths to the street.

interventions.title: Shared Street Treatment
interventions.description: If a sidewalk cannot be built, implement a 'woonerf' or shared street design with heavy traffic calming and distinct paving to prioritize pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Installing street trees or large planters would provide a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and the roadway.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Implementing speed humps or cushions would help maintain low vehicle speeds appropriate for a residential street.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffers
interventions.description: Introduce street trees or a planting strip between the sidewalk and the curb to provide a safety buffer and improve the pedestrian experience.

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing and Markings
interventions.description: Apply paint to define travel lanes and parking lanes, narrowing the perceived roadway to slow traffic.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Clearance and Maintenance
interventions.description: Remove debris and household items to restore a continuous, accessible path for pedestrians and ensure ADA compliance.
